agenda: The situation in the Middle East; Letter dated 15 October 2025 from the Panel of Experts on Yemen addressed to the President of the Security Council (S/2025/650)
penholder: United Kingdom of Great Britain and Northern Ireland
members: United Kingdom of Great Britain and Northern Ireland

steps.by: United Kingdom of Great Britain and Northern Ireland
steps.intent: The United Kingdom’s objective is to secure a consensus renewal of the Yemen sanctions and Panel of Experts mandates while reinforcing maritime security, arms-embargo implementation, humanitarian access and women, peace and security. The text has been kept technical and balanced to avoid a veto, but difficult negotiations are expected over references to Houthi attacks on Israel, the detention of vessels and crews, and any language that could be read as new maritime enforcement authority. We also anticipate Russian and Chinese scrutiny of accountability and arms-smuggling language, and will resist dilution of the Panel’s reporting mandate.

messages.Algeria: Algeria supports renewal of the sanctions regime and the Panel of Experts’ mandate, but the text must be balanced and grounded in international law. We ask the penholder to condemn all attacks on civilians and civilian infrastructure in Yemen, including Israeli airstrikes, and to make the demand in OP2 apply to all parties while preserving a specific demand on the Houthis. We also seek stronger humanitarian carve-outs so that sanctions do not impede delivery of assistance.
messages.China: China supports the renewal of the Yemen sanctions regime and the Panel of Experts mandate. The draft should be more balanced and should not condemn only one side while ignoring military strikes against Yemen. We therefore ask for the proposed amendments to PP6 and OP2, and a minor addition to OP3 on external interference.
messages.Denmark: Denmark welcomes the draft and supports renewal of the sanctions and Panel of Experts mandate. We would like OP4 to cover all arbitrarily detained persons and OP6 to reaffirm humanitarian principles and impartial access. We also suggest strengthening OP3 on women's full, equal and meaningful participation.
messages.France: France supports the renewal of the Yemen sanctions regime and the Panel of Experts’ mandate and considers this draft a good basis. We would like the text to reflect more clearly the full range of Houthi cross-border attacks and to strengthen implementation of the targeted arms embargo, including with respect to external actors and maritime transfers. We also suggest recalling that there is no military solution to the conflict. These are constructive amendments, and we are ready to work with the penholder.
messages.Greece: Greece supports the draft and the renewal of the Yemen sanctions and Panel of Experts mandate. As a maritime and shipping nation, we ask that OP2 and OP8 state more explicitly the need to protect seafarers, critical maritime infrastructure and freedom of navigation under international law, including UNCLOS. We also ask that OP3 reflect the full, equal and meaningful participation of women. With these adjustments, Greece can support the text.
messages.Guyana: Guyana supports the renewal of the 2140/2216 sanctions regime and the Panel of Experts mandate, and thanks the United Kingdom for its consultative approach. As part of the A3+, we ask for a new preambular paragraph welcoming the Gaza ceasefire and the halt in Houthi attacks on shipping since 5 October, and calling for sustained regional de-escalation. We also propose minor amendments to OP6 to refer explicitly to the United Nations humanitarian principles and to rapid humanitarian access. These changes would strengthen the text’s humanitarian and regional de-escalation dimensions without altering its core.
messages.Pakistan: Pakistan supports the renewal of the 2140/2216 measures and the Panel of Experts' mandate, and welcomes the draft's humanitarian and political elements. To ensure balance and reflect the gravity of recent Israeli strikes on Yemen, we request a new preambular paragraph condemning those attacks and calling for their cessation. We can join consensus if this balance is reflected in the text.
messages.Panama: Panama supports the renewal of the Yemen sanctions regime and the Panel of Experts mandate and welcomes the United Kingdom's balanced text. As a maritime nation, we ask that the draft expressly reaffirm freedom of navigation and transit passage in the Red Sea, Gulf of Aden and Bab al-Mandab and reflect that in OP2. We also seek a minor strengthening of OP14 to make the humanitarian exemption process timely and transparent, consistent with the Council's repeated commitment that sanctions not harm civilians.
messages.Republic of Korea: The Republic of Korea supports the renewal of the sanctions regime and the Panel's mandate and thanks the United Kingdom for a balanced draft. As Chair of the 2140 Committee, we ask that OP7 require possible violations to be reported to the Committee in a timely manner, and that OP2 expressly call for respect for freedom of navigation in the Red Sea, Gulf of Aden and Bab al-Mandab. These changes would strengthen implementation and maritime security without altering the text's balance.
messages.Russian Federation: The Russian Federation supports the renewal of the Yemen sanctions regime and the Panel of Experts mandate as a technical rollover. However, the text must not create any new authority for interdiction at sea or for an expansive interpretation of the arms embargo. We also ask the penholder to balance the condemnations and to avoid language that could be read as endorsing external military strikes against Yemen. With these adjustments, we are ready to support the draft.
messages.Sierra Leone: Sierra Leone supports the draft as circulated. It reflects the Council's prior consensus on Yemen's sovereignty, humanitarian access, women, peace and security, and accountability, and renews the sanctions and Panel mandate needed to address arms diversion and maritime threats. We urge all members to preserve consensus and adopt the text without weakening its humanitarian carve-out or protection provisions.
messages.Slovenia: Slovenia thanks the United Kingdom for the balanced draft and supports renewal of the sanctions and Panel mandate. We ask for stronger WPS language in OP3 and an explicit call to protect civilians and civilian objects in OP6. We would also welcome a minor addition to OP12 ensuring the Panel continues reporting on conflict-related sexual violence and violations against children.
messages.Somalia: Somalia supports the draft and thanks the United Kingdom for a balanced text. Given our exposure to Red Sea and Bab al-Mandab shipping, we ask that OP2 expressly affirm freedom of navigation and safe passage for commercial and humanitarian vessels, and that OP8 reference UNCLOS. We also wish to see the humanitarian exemption language in OP14 preserved intact.
messages.United States of America: The United States supports a clean renewal of the sanctions regime and the Panel of Experts mandate, and we thank the United Kingdom for its drafting. We ask that the text more clearly assign responsibility to the Houthis and their Iranian backers, strengthen the arms-embargo language from concern to condemnation, and explicitly call for the release of current and former locally employed U.S. Embassy staff in Sana'a.

steps.summary: The revision incorporates the broad consensus by retaining strong Houthi condemnation and maritime security while adding balanced generic language on external strikes and sovereignty, accepting Russia's high-seas inspection caveat, and strengthening humanitarian, WPS and reporting provisions. It also reflects key US, French, Gulf and maritime priorities. The United Kingdom expects broad support, with possible abstentions on balance language.

messages.Algeria: We thank the penholder for revision 1 and for partially reflecting our concerns. However, the text still lacks an explicit condemnation of Israeli strikes on Yemen, and OP2 remains framed in a one-sided manner. We therefore ask that PP10 name the Israeli strikes and that OP2 be reformulated to demand cessation by all parties while retaining specific demands on the Houthis. Algeria can support the renewal once these balance and sovereignty concerns are addressed.
messages.China: China supports the renewal of the Yemen sanctions regime and the Panel of Experts mandate, and appreciates the penholder's partial incorporation of our earlier concerns on sovereignty and external interference. To preserve Council unity and avoid unilateral or country-specific attributions, we ask that OP2 refer to 'the Houthis' rather than 'the Houthi terrorist group', and that PP9 delete 'including from Iran' and instead refer to transfers 'from any source'. With these changes, China is prepared to support the draft.
messages.Denmark: Denmark thanks the penholder for incorporating our earlier suggestions on arbitrary detention, humanitarian principles and the full, equal and meaningful participation of women, youth and civil society. We support the current text and believe it strikes the right balance in condemning Houthi attacks, upholding Yemen’s sovereignty and territorial integrity, strengthening maritime security and arms-embargo implementation, and prioritizing humanitarian access and accountability. Denmark encourages all Council members to unite behind this resolution and to focus on its full implementation.
messages.France: France welcomes the revised text and thanks the penholder for accommodating our priorities on Houthi attacks, arms-embargo enforcement and external actors. The draft maintains the necessary balance on Yemen's sovereignty, humanitarian access and the UN-led political process. We will vote in favour and encourage all Council members to support the text.
messages.Greece: Greece supports the current text as revised and thanks the United Kingdom for its constructive penholdership. We welcome the incorporation of our priority concerns on seafarers, freedom of navigation, UNCLOS, critical maritime infrastructure and the full, equal and meaningful participation of women. The text is balanced and operational, and Greece calls on all Council members to join consensus for its swift adoption.
messages.Guyana: Guyana supports the revised draft and welcomes the incorporation of our earlier proposals on the Gaza ceasefire and humanitarian access. We would still like OP3 to retain an explicit call for an immediate nationwide ceasefire, which remains essential for humanitarian access and a credible political process. With that change, Guyana is ready to vote in favour of the resolution.
messages.Pakistan: We welcome the addition of a preambular paragraph addressing all military strikes against Yemen, including against civilian infrastructure and ports, which partially addresses our concern. While we would have preferred an explicit condemnation of Israeli attacks, we recognize the current text as a compromise. In the interest of Council unity and the renewal of the sanctions and Panel mandate, Pakistan supports the draft as it stands.
messages.Panama: Panama welcomes the revised text and thanks the United Kingdom for incorporating our key maritime security concerns, including the new preambular reference to freedom of navigation and transit passage, the OP2 language on UNCLOS and shipping safety, and the OP15 transparency provisions. We also value the reaffirmation in OP9 that resolutions 2140 (2014) and 2216 (2015) do not authorize high-seas inspections without flag State consent. Panama supports the draft as it stands and looks forward to its adoption by consensus.
messages.Republic of Korea: The Republic of Korea thanks the United Kingdom for incorporating our earlier suggestions on timely reporting in OP8 and freedom of navigation in OP2. The text maintains a balanced and robust response: it condemns Houthi attacks, strengthens implementation of the targeted arms embargo, and preserves humanitarian safeguards. As Chair of the Yemen Sanctions Committee, we believe the draft provides a solid basis for Council unity, and the Republic of Korea supports its adoption as it stands.
messages.Russian Federation: We thank the penholder for reflecting the key Russian caveats on high-seas inspection and on avoiding political pressure through sanctions. However, the continued singling out of Israel in the Houthi condemnation unbalances the text and conflates separate conflicts. We ask that the reference to Israel be removed from PP7 and OP2, while retaining the generic condemnation of attacks on civilians and civilian infrastructure in the region. With that adjustment, the Russian Federation is prepared to support the resolution.
messages.Sierra Leone: Sierra Leone supports the revised draft as a balanced basis for consensus. We welcome the retention of the humanitarian carve-out, the clear reaffirmation of Yemen's sovereignty and territorial integrity, and the renewal of the Panel of Experts' mandate. We encourage all Council members to unite behind the text so that the Council can speak with one voice on Yemen.
messages.Slovenia: Slovenia thanks the United Kingdom for its able facilitation and for incorporating our earlier requests on WPS language in OP3, protection of civilians and civilian objects in OP7, and CRSV and children reporting in OP13. The text is balanced, reaffirms Yemen's sovereignty and territorial integrity, and strengthens humanitarian access and accountability. We support the draft as it stands and call for its adoption.
messages.Somalia: Somalia thanks the United Kingdom for its leadership and for incorporating our earlier requests on freedom of navigation and UNCLOS, while preserving the humanitarian carve-out. We support the current text as balanced and consistent with Somalia’s commitment to Yemen’s sovereignty, territorial integrity, humanitarian access and an inclusive UN-led political process. We encourage all Council members to unite behind the draft and to ensure its full implementation.
messages.United States of America: The United States supports the current text as revised. We thank the United Kingdom for incorporating our priorities: condemning Iran's weapons transfers to the Houthis, using the designation 'Houthi terrorist group,' demanding the release of U.S. Embassy staff, strengthening arms-embargo language, and protecting journalists. We urge the Council to adopt it without delay.

The UK retains the core Houthi condemnation, Iran attribution, terrorist designation and Israel references to preserve US and UK priorities; Algeria, China and Russia are expected to abstain rather than veto.

reasons.Algeria: Algeria has consistently supported Yemen-related mandate renewals and arms-embargo measures while criticising unbalanced Council texts. Its important requested changes were rejected, but the resolution still renews the Panel and sanctions regime, so Algeria would vote in favour with reservations rather than abstain.
reasons.China: China supports renewing the Yemen sanctions and Panel mandate, but its important requests on removing the “terrorist group” designation and the Iran attribution were rejected, so abstention best reflects its balanced and non-attribution position. A veto would be disproportionate given its support for the renewal itself.
reasons.Denmark: Denmark consistently supports UN-led Yemen peace efforts, humanitarian access, arms-embargo enforcement, and accountability, and the UK draft aligns with these priorities. No red lines or changes were required, so Denmark votes in favour.
reasons.France: France has consistently supported renewal of the Yemen sanctions and Panel of Experts mandate and the UK-led text; supporting it advances France's priorities on maritime security, arms-embargo enforcement, humanitarian access, and a UN-led political process without crossing any red lines.
reasons.Greece: Greece aligns with the draft’s emphasis on maritime security, UNCLOS, humanitarian access, arms embargo enforcement and a UN-led Yemeni political process, and it had already signalled support with no requested changes. With its EU/NATO and regional partnerships and concern over Houthi attacks on shipping and Israel, Greece would vote in favour.
reasons.Guyana: Guyana has consistently supported renewing the Yemen sanctions regime and Panel of Experts mandate, and its key requested OP3 amendment on an immediate nationwide ceasefire was accepted. It will vote yes while emphasizing sovereignty, humanitarian access, accountability and de-escalation.
reasons.Pakistan: Pakistan supported the draft in negotiations and has consistently backed renewal of the Yemen sanctions/Panel of Experts mandate while emphasizing Yemeni sovereignty, humanitarian access and a UN-led political process. A favourable vote is consistent with its Gulf ties, maritime-security concerns and Council record.
reasons.Panama: Panama was recorded as supporting the draft, made no requests, and its foreign policy favours peaceful settlement, international law, humanitarian access and maritime security. The resolution aligns with those priorities, so Panama votes in favour.
reasons.Republic of Korea: ROK has consistently supported renewing the Yemen sanctions regime and Panel mandate, and the draft aligns with its interests in maritime security, nonproliferation, humanitarian access, and a UN-led political process. No red lines were raised, so ROK votes yes.
reasons.Russian Federation: Russia has consistently supported recent Yemen sanctions renewals despite objections, valuing Council unity and the Panel's mandate. The draft includes key Russian priorities such as no high-seas inspections without flag State consent and calls on external parties to respect Yemen's sovereignty, making a yes vote likely with a statement expressing concerns.
reasons.Sierra Leone: Sierra Leone has consistently voted in favour of Council resolutions on Yemen and supported this UK-led draft without requesting changes. The text aligns with Sierra Leone’s priorities on peace, humanitarian access, sovereignty and international law, so it should vote yes.
reasons.Slovenia: Slovenia supported the draft in the last negotiation round without requesting changes and has consistently voted in favor of renewing Yemen sanctions and the Panel of Experts mandate. Its statement reinforces its established priorities: international law, civilian protection, humanitarian access, accountability, and women’s participation.
reasons.Somalia: Somalia has consistently supported recent Yemen resolutions and had no changes requested; the draft aligns with its priorities on Yemen’s sovereignty, Red Sea maritime security, arms-embargo implementation and humanitarian access.
reasons.United Kingdom of Great Britain and Nort: The United Kingdom is the penholder and would vote in favour of its own balanced draft, using a pre-vote statement to urge Council unity and highlight key priorities.
reasons.United States of America: The United States supports the UK draft, which aligns with its priorities on Houthi attacks, Iran’s arms transfers, maritime security, humanitarian access, and renewal of sanctions and the Panel of Experts. No veto or abstention is warranted.

before.Algeria:
Algeria will vote in favour of this resolution, including the renewal of the targeted arms embargo and the mandate of the Panel of Experts, because we support every effort to prevent the illicit transfer of weapons, to preserve Yemen’s unity and territorial integrity, and to advance a Yemeni-led political process under United Nations auspices.

At the same time, my delegation regrets that the text remains unbalanced in important respects. We had sought explicit condemnation of the Israeli airstrikes against Sana’a, Hudaydah and al-Jawf, which have caused civilian casualties, and a formulation demanding that all parties cease attacks on commercial and civilian vessels and all cross-border attacks. Those concerns were not retained.

Algeria therefore stresses that this resolution must not be read as legitimising any military action that violates Yemen’s sovereignty, independence and territorial integrity. We call for an immediate cessation of all attacks against civilians and civilian infrastructure, for full respect for international law and freedom of navigation, and for unhindered humanitarian access. A durable settlement in Yemen requires dialogue, national sovereignty and an end to external interference.
before.China:
Mr. President,

China supports the renewal of the sanctions measures and the mandate of the Panel of Experts on Yemen. We support an inclusive, Yemeni-led and Yemeni-owned political process under United Nations auspices, respect for Yemen’s sovereignty, independence and territorial integrity, and the need to address the humanitarian situation and ensure freedom of navigation.

At the same time, China has serious concerns about certain language in this draft. In particular, the use of the designation “terrorist group” for the Houthis and the attribution of arms transfers specifically to Iran are not conducive to an impartial, balanced and objective approach. Such language may complicate dialogue, regional de-escalation and the broader political process. These matters should be handled on the basis of verified information and through consultation among all relevant parties.

China therefore will abstain on this draft resolution.
before.Denmark: Denmark will vote in favour of this resolution. We thank the United Kingdom for its efforts to produce a balanced text that renews the sanctions regime and the mandate of the Panel of Experts, which remain essential tools in support of a political settlement in Yemen. Denmark remains deeply concerned by attacks on shipping and civilians, violations of the targeted arms embargo, the humanitarian crisis, arbitrary detentions, and violations of international humanitarian law and human rights. We underline the need for unhindered humanitarian access, accountability, protection of civilians, and the full, equal and meaningful participation of women in the political process. This resolution sends a clear message that all parties must de-escalate, respect Yemen’s sovereignty and territorial integrity, release those arbitrarily detained, and engage constructively with the Special Envoy towards an inclusive, Yemeni-led political solution.
before.France: France votes in favour of this resolution. We thank the United Kingdom for its work. Renewing the targeted measures and the mandate of the Panel of Experts is essential to counter illicit arms transfers to the Houthis, support maritime security in the Red Sea and Gulf of Aden, and create the conditions for a credible political process. France condemns Houthi attacks on commercial and civilian vessels and cross-border attacks against Saudi Arabia, the United Arab Emirates and Israel. We call for the immediate release of all arbitrarily detained personnel, including United Nations staff and the crews of the MV Galaxy Leader and the MV Rawabee. France remains deeply concerned by the humanitarian situation and calls for unconditional, safe and unhindered humanitarian access, protection of civilians and civilian infrastructure, and full respect for Yemen's sovereignty, independence and territorial integrity. We welcome the ceasefire in Gaza and the halt in Houthi attacks since 5 October, and we urge all actors to preserve de-escalation. There can be no military solution. The only viable path is an inclusive Yemeni-led and Yemeni-owned political process under United Nations auspices, with the full, equal and meaningful participation of women. France will continue to support the Special Envoy and the full implementation of the arms embargo, while ensuring that the sanctions regime does not harm humanitarian access.
before.Greece: Thank you, President. Greece thanks the United Kingdom for its efforts in steering this text. Greece will vote in favour of the draft resolution. We do so because it reaffirms the unity, sovereignty, independence and territorial integrity of Yemen, and because it responds clearly to the grave threat posed to maritime security and freedom of navigation in the Red Sea, Gulf of Aden and Bab al-Mandab. Attacks on commercial and civilian vessels, the detention of crews and cross-border attacks are unacceptable and must cease. Greece also strongly supports the demand for unconditional, safe and unhindered humanitarian access, the protection of civilians, the full implementation of the targeted arms embargo, accountability for violations of international law, and a genuine United Nations-led political process with the full, equal and meaningful participation of women. At the same time, we stress that all parties and external actors must respect Yemen’s sovereignty and territorial integrity, avoid actions that exacerbate the humanitarian situation, and seize the opportunity presented by the current de-escalation to pursue a durable political settlement.
before.Guyana: Guyana thanks the penholder for its constructive engagement and for accepting the important amendment to operative paragraph 3, which now clearly calls for an immediate nationwide ceasefire. Guyana will vote in favour of this resolution. We do so because the sanctions regime and the mandate of the Panel of Experts remain essential tools for accountability, for curbing illicit arms flows, and for supporting a political settlement in Yemen. At the same time, we stress that this resolution must be implemented in full respect for Yemen’s sovereignty, unity, independence and territorial integrity, and with the protection of civilians and unhindered humanitarian access at its centre. We call on all parties to de-escalate, comply with international law, release all arbitrarily detained personnel, and engage constructively with the Special Envoy without preconditions. The humanitarian exemptions and safeguards in the text must also be applied promptly and transparently so that the civilian population does not bear the cost of sanctions. Guyana remains committed to an inclusive, Yemeni-led and Yemeni-owned political process under United Nations auspices.
before.Pakistan: Mr. President, Pakistan thanks the penholder for the consultative process. We vote in favour of this resolution because it reaffirms Yemen’s unity, sovereignty, independence and territorial integrity and supports a peaceful, inclusive and Yemeni-led political settlement under United Nations auspices. Pakistan remains deeply concerned by the humanitarian situation in Yemen, by threats to maritime security in the Red Sea, Gulf of Aden and Bab al-Mandab, including attacks on commercial and civilian vessels, and by continued violations of the targeted arms embargo. At the same time, all military actions must respect Yemen’s sovereignty and international law, and sanctions and counter-terrorism measures must not impede humanitarian access or exacerbate the suffering of civilians. The only sustainable solution is dialogue, de-escalation, a nationwide ceasefire and constructive engagement with the Special Envoy, including the full, equal and meaningful participation of women in the political process. Pakistan will therefore support this resolution and calls for its balanced and non-politicized implementation in the service of peace and stability in Yemen and the wider region.
before.Panama: Panama will vote in favour of the draft resolution. We do so because it reaffirms the unity, sovereignty, independence and territorial integrity of Yemen, supports an inclusive Yemeni-led political process under United Nations auspices, and calls for de-escalation, humanitarian access and the protection of civilians. Panama also attaches importance to the renewal of the targeted sanctions and the mandate of the Panel of Experts, as well as to the call for full respect for international law, including freedom of navigation and the safety of seafarers in the Red Sea, Gulf of Aden and Bab al-Mandab. We encourage all parties to engage constructively with the Special Envoy and to pursue dialogue as the only viable path towards lasting peace.
before.Republic of Korea: Thank you, Mr. President. The Republic of Korea will vote in favour of this draft resolution. We thank the United Kingdom for its leadership and all Council members for their constructive engagement. The renewal of the Yemen sanctions regime and the Panel of Experts mandate is essential to address continued violations of the targeted arms embargo, including illicit transfers of weapons and components to the Houthis, and to respond to threats to maritime security in the Red Sea and Gulf of Aden. At the same time, we stress that sanctions must not impede humanitarian assistance. We therefore welcome the resolution's clear call for safe and unhindered humanitarian access, protection of civilians, and an inclusive Yemeni-led political process under United Nations auspices. We urge all Member States to implement the sanctions measures fully and to cooperate with the Panel of Experts. The Republic of Korea remains committed to supporting peace, stability and freedom of navigation in the region.
before.Russian Federation: Mr. President, the Russian Federation will vote in favour of the draft resolution renewing the sanctions regime and the mandate of the Panel of Experts on Yemen. We support the extension because we believe it is important to preserve the Council's unity and to maintain a mechanism that can provide objective information to support a political settlement. At the same time, we regret that the penholder did not take into account our proposals to remove references to Israel from the description of Houthi cross-border attacks. We believe that language should be balanced and should not complicate efforts to sustain the Gaza ceasefire. We also stress that the sanctions must not be used as an instrument of political pressure, and we welcome the reaffirmation in paragraph 9 that the resolutions do not authorize inspection of vessels on the high seas without the consent of the flag State. We call on all parties to exercise restraint and to engage constructively with the Special Envoy.
before.Sierra Leone: Sierra Leone votes in favour of this draft resolution. We support the renewal of the sanctions measures and the Panel of Experts mandate, and we welcome the Council’s clear message against attacks on commercial and civilian shipping, civilians and civilian infrastructure. At the same time, we stress that Yemen’s sovereignty, independence and territorial integrity must be respected, that all external military actions causing civilian harm must cease, and that humanitarian access must be unconditional, safe, rapid and unhindered. We call on all parties to engage constructively with the Special Envoy, ensure the full, equal and meaningful participation of women, and release all arbitrarily detained United Nations and humanitarian personnel. We also underscore that the sanctions regime must not have adverse humanitarian consequences for the Yemeni people, and that implementation of the arms embargo must be consistent with international law, including the United Nations Convention on the Law of the Sea.
before.Slovenia: Slovenia will vote in favour of this resolution. We support the renewal of the targeted sanctions regime and the mandate of the Panel of Experts on Yemen, which remain important tools for supporting a political settlement and upholding the arms embargo. We underline the need for all parties to respect Yemen’s sovereignty, unity, independence and territorial integrity, to protect civilians, and to ensure unconditional, safe and unhindered humanitarian access. We call for the immediate release of all arbitrarily detained United Nations personnel, humanitarian workers and civilians, and we stress that accountability for violations of international humanitarian law and human rights law, including sexual and gender-based violence and recruitment of children, must be pursued. We also reiterate the importance of the full, equal and meaningful participation of women in Yemen’s political process.
before.Somalia: Mr. President, Somalia will vote in favour of this draft resolution. We thank the United Kingdom for its efforts and believe the text is balanced and constructive. Somalia reaffirms its support for the unity, sovereignty, independence and territorial integrity of Yemen and for a Yemeni-led political process under United Nations auspices. We condemn attacks on commercial and civilian vessels and on civilians and civilian infrastructure, and we stress the importance of freedom of navigation in the Red Sea, Gulf of Aden and Bab al-Mandab. We also support the renewal of the targeted arms embargo and the Panel of Experts’ mandate, and we call on all Member States to implement those measures fully. At the same time, we underscore the need for unconditional humanitarian access, protection of civilians and respect for Yemen’s sovereignty, and we urge all parties to de-escalate and sustain the current cessation of attacks. Somalia supports the release of all arbitrarily detained United Nations personnel, humanitarian workers and civilians as demanded in the text.
before.United Kingdom of Great Britain and Nort: Thank you, Mr President. The United Kingdom has tabled this draft to renew the Yemen sanctions regime and the mandate of the Panel of Experts, to reinforce the demand that the Houthis cease attacks on shipping, civilians and neighbouring states, release detained vessels and personnel, and comply with the targeted arms embargo. The text is balanced: it also addresses humanitarian access, accountability, the protection of civilians, and the need for an inclusive Yemeni-led political process under United Nations auspices. We call on all Council members to support it.
before.United States of America: Thank you, Mr. President. The United States will vote in favour of this resolution. We strongly support its clear condemnation of Houthi attacks on commercial and civilian vessels, civilians and civilian infrastructure, and cross-border attacks; its demand that all seized vessels and crews be released; and its recognition of the continued threat posed by illicit arms transfers to the Houthis, including from Iran. We welcome the Gaza ceasefire and the halt in Houthi attacks since 5 October, and we call on the Houthis to sustain de-escalation and respect freedom of navigation. The United States remains committed to Yemen’s sovereignty, unity and territorial integrity, to unhindered humanitarian access, and to a Yemeni-led political process under United Nations auspices. We also underscore that this resolution does not affect the inherent right of States to self-defence or the imperative of countering terrorism. We urge all parties to comply fully with this resolution and urge the Council to remain unified.

after.China:
Mr. President,

China abstained on the draft resolution just adopted. China supports the renewal of the Yemen sanctions regime and the mandate of the Panel of Experts. We support a Yemeni-led and Yemeni-owned political process under United Nations auspices, respect for Yemen’s sovereignty, independence and territorial integrity, unhindered humanitarian access, and freedom of navigation in the Red Sea and Gulf of Aden.

At the same time, China has serious concerns about certain language in the text. In particular, the designation of the Houthis as a “terrorist group” and the attribution of arms transfers specifically to Iran are not conducive to an impartial, balanced and objective approach. Such language risks politicizing the work of the Panel of Experts, complicating regional de-escalation and undermining the broader political process. These matters should be handled on the basis of verified information and through dialogue, not through unsubstantiated attribution or pressure.

China’s abstention does not mean that we endorse continued attacks on commercial and civilian vessels, cross-border attacks, or violations of the arms embargo. We call on all parties to cease hostilities, exercise restraint, engage with the Special Envoy, and create conditions for a comprehensive political settlement. China will continue to play a constructive role in promoting peace and stability in Yemen and the region.
after.United Kingdom of Great Britain and Nort:
Mr President,

The United Kingdom welcomes the adoption of this resolution. I thank Council members for their constructive engagement and for the broad support it has received. We also note China’s abstention and appreciate its engagement throughout the negotiations; the United Kingdom will continue to work with China and all Council members on the implementation of this mandate.

This resolution renews the targeted sanctions regime and the mandate of the Panel of Experts at a critical moment. It sends an unambiguous message that Houthi attacks on commercial and civilian vessels in the Red Sea, Gulf of Aden and Bab al-Mandab, on civilians and civilian infrastructure, and cross-border attacks must cease immediately; that seized vessels and crews must be released; and that the targeted arms embargo must be fully implemented. The Panel’s reporting remains essential to identifying violations and to holding accountable those who fuel this conflict.

The United Kingdom remains equally committed to the humanitarian and political dimensions of this crisis. The resolution rightly calls for unconditional, safe and unhindered humanitarian access, protection of civilians, accountability for violations of international humanitarian law and human rights law, and the full, equal and meaningful participation of women in the political process. We underscore that the sanctions measures are not intended to harm the civilian population or to impede humanitarian assistance, commercial imports or remittances.

There is no military solution to the conflict in Yemen. We call on all parties to engage constructively and without preconditions with the Special Envoy of the Secretary-General and to pursue an inclusive, Yemeni-led and Yemeni-owned political process under United Nations auspices. All parties must respect Yemen’s sovereignty, unity, independence and territorial integrity and comply with their obligations under international law.

The United Kingdom will continue to support the Council’s efforts to sustain de-escalation, including in the wake of the Gaza ceasefire, and to ensure that this resolution is implemented in full.
